text.content:
Welcome to Mind's Eye Theatre: Laws of the Night for Foundry VTT — an unofficial fan system for playing the trait-bidding, Rock-Paper-Scissors style of Vampire the Masquerade LARP online.

This guide gets a new table up and running. Read the pages in order; players mainly need Creating a Character and Traits & Challenges, Storytellers should also read Storyteller Quick-Start.

What's in the box

  • Compendiums for every character option — Clans & Bloodlines, Disciplines & Powers, Abilities, Backgrounds, Merits & Flaws, Paths, Derangements, Gear — plus sample NPCs and rules reference.
  • A Character Builder wizard that walks you through creation with live point/freebie budgeting.
  • A Challenge tool for resolving trait bids and gestures, with retests and a Storyteller dashboard.

The fastest way to make a character is the Character Builder. Open the Actors sidebar and click the Character Builder button at the top. (Any player can use it — the character it creates is owned by whoever built it.)

Step by step

  1. Concept — name, Generation, Clan, Sect, Path, Nature/Demeanor. Picking a Clan auto-fills its three in-clan Disciplines (you can swap any of them).
  2. Attributes — split 15 across Physical / Social / Mental (7/5/3). Priority is set automatically from the highest.
  3. Abilities, Disciplines, Backgrounds, Virtues — click entries to add them and set their dots. The header shows a live Freebie XP total the whole time.
  4. Merits & Flaws, Derangement — Flaws grant Freebies (max 7); a Derangement grants +2.
  5. Review — anything over an area's base allotment (plus Merits) is paid from Freebies. To spend Freebie XP, use Back to any panel and raise a trait past its base — the header total updates live.

Every choice has an info button and a hover tooltip that opens or previews its compendium entry, so you don't need the rulebook open beside you.

Prefer to build by hand? Create a Character actor directly and drag options from the compendiums onto the sheet. Discipline powers pull in learning order as you set dots.

MET is resolved by bidding Traits and throwing a Rock-Paper-Scissors gesture, not by rolling dice.

Traits

Your Attributes are pools of Traits (Physical, Social, Mental). On the sheet, Trait chips toggle between available and spent. You bid Traits to win challenges; retests and losses spend them.

Making a challenge

  1. Open your sheet and click Challenge (or use a Power's challenge button).
  2. Pick the challenge type (Physical/Social/Mental) and your target. Add any bonus/penalty Traits.
  3. Both sides throw a gesture. The tool logs the bids, gestures and result to chat. Ties compare Traits; a further tie can go to a Trait bid-off.

Because play is online, the responder throws on their own screen — the challenger never sees the opposing gesture early. You resolve someone else's challenge by responding to the prompt in chat.

Health & Willpower

The health track cycles Ok → Bashing → Lethal → Aggravated by clicking the boxes. Willpower and Blood are tracked on the sheet and seeded from your Generation.

As GM you get extra tools. A ST Panel button sits on screen (and in scene controls).

Storyteller Panel

  • Run surprise, forced and coin-toss challenges.
  • Apply named trait-modifier effects (temporary bonuses/penalties) to characters — they flow into challenge bids automatically.
  • Apply Afflictions; players can clear them from their own sheet if you forget.

Running the table

  • The Active Challenges dashboard tracks every challenge in flight across the session.
  • Right-click any compendium entry → Post to Chat to share a rule, power or lore snippet.
  • Sample NPCs (Camarilla, Sabbat, Anarch, city books, mortals & ghouls) are ready to drag onto scenes.
  • Initiative is a flat d20 draw (MET breaks order randomly, not by stat).
  • NPC auto-answer: on any NPC, tick Auto-answer challenges (header) and that NPC responds to Challenges automatically with a random gesture — still bidding its real Trait pool, and re-throwing on retests — so you do not have to answer each one. Add can throw Bomb to include Bomb in its random pool.

Permissions

If you want players to create their own characters directly, enable Create New Actors for the Player role in Game Settings → Configure Permissions. Otherwise the Character Builder hands finished characters to an online Storyteller to create, keeping the player as owner.
